properties.name: The remote client measures the folder's own files (combined position 7)
properties.rationale: A design on a server holds no tree, so until now every file-evidence call from a remote client was either refused by name or took the agent's typed hash on faith (flo2's combined position 2 made the server accept the caller's evidence; this turns that evidence from the agent's word into a measurement the client takes). The root is never guessed: no .reflow2.toml folder and no --tree-root means nothing measured and the reply says so, because a checksum measured under the wrong folder is worse than none. Observed failing first: six of the seven end-to-end tests failed on main's client (the server refused the checksum-less calls), all seven pass at f792e88dc. Not in this step: loop_status's artifacts block (a server surface change) and extra roots. Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_019Xbw6PG9mXJiU2Sb421fnq
properties.subject: system
properties.summary: Combined plan position 7 built: the person's own reflow2-mcp client, attached through a folder's .reflow2.toml or given --tree-root, measures the folder's files for link_artifact, set_artifact_checksum, set_artifact_checksums and reconcile_artifacts with the server's own measuring code and sends the checksums; a tree-less server (flo2.io, a registry) records them as asserted and the reply says they were measured on this machine by the client, under which root. New module crates/reflow2-mcp/src/client_measure.rs; proxy.rs's run_remote(_with_notice) take the root and the per-line task screens, measures, forwards and rewrites the reply; main.rs passes the root in both client modes. Additive: nothing on the wire changes for anyone else, the server is untouched.
